blogs.title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) — The TL;DR for Practitioners
blogs.description: A friendly, non‑math walkthrough of the DPO idea: why current RLHF pipelines are complex, how DPO reparameterizes the reward-to-policy mapping, and why that means you can train a preference‑aligned LM with a simple cross‑entropy loss. Includes intuitive diagrams, a comparison table vs PPO/REINFORCE, and guidance for when DPO is a good fit. Target audience: ML engineers and students.

blogs.title: Implementing DPO: A Step‑by‑Step Code Tutorial
blogs.description: Hands‑on tutorial that walks through implementing DPO end‑to‑end on an open dataset (e.g., TL;DR or a toy sentiment setup). Includes data preparation for preference pairs, building the reference model, computing the DPO loss, practical batching considerations, and lightweight training tips. Code snippets in PyTorch/Hugging Face-style pseudo‑code and suggested hyperparameters for small/medium models.

blogs.title: DPO vs PPO: Practical Benchmarks, Costs and When to Use Each
blogs.description: A pragmatic benchmarking post comparing performance, stability, and compute cost of DPO against PPO-based RLHF across typical tasks (sentiment control, summarization, dialogue). Explains why DPO often outperforms PPO in reward/KL tradeoffs, highlights failure modes of actor‑critic approaches, and gives a decision checklist for choosing DPO or PPO in production.

blogs.title: Your LM Is a Reward Model — Why That Changes How We Think About Alignment
blogs.description: Explores the conceptual implication from the paper that a policy parameterization implicitly defines a reward function (and vice versa). Covers under‑specification in preference models, what that means for interpretability and debugging, and concrete diagnostic techniques to inspect an LM's implicit rewards. Written for researchers and thoughtful practitioners.

blogs.title: DPO for Non‑Text Generative Models: Opportunities and Challenges
blogs.description: A forward‑looking post that translates DPO's principles to other modalities (images, audio, code generation). Discusses what needs to change (sampling, reference policies, preference collection), potential advantages (simpler training loops) and pitfalls (high‑dimensional action spaces, human labeling costs). Good for ML teams exploring multimodal alignment.

blogs.title: Hyperparameters, Beta and Degeneration: Practical Tips to Stabilize DPO Training
blogs.description: Focused guide on the most important practical knobs in DPO (the beta KL weight, reference model initialization, batch composition, learning rate, handling unlikelihood terms). Also covers common failure modes (mode collapse, over‑optimization) and simple diagnostics to recover. Targets ML practitioners running experiments.

blogs.title: Evaluating Preference‑Trained Models — From GPT‑4 Proxies to Human Studies
blogs.description: A practical primer on how to evaluate models trained with preferences. Covers pros/cons of using LLMs (GPT‑4) as automatic judges, how to validate automated evaluations with human annotation, designing win‑rate experiments, and tips for prompt design for consistent judgments. Useful for ML teams and product owners.

blogs.title: From Research to Product: Integrating DPO into an ML Ops Pipeline
blogs.description: Operational guide for taking DPO from experiment to production: data collection loops for preferences, continuous retraining, reference policy management, monitoring KL drift, A/B testing strategies, and cost implications. Also touches on safety review checkpoints and rollback strategies. Targeted at ML engineers and product managers.

blogs.title: Mini Case Study: Using DPO to Control Sentiment and Tone
blogs.description: Walkthrough of a compact case study where DPO is used to control sentiment and tone in responses (movie reviews, customer support examples). Shows dataset creation (automatic vs human prefs), training curves, examples of before/after generations, and lessons learned on generalization and fine‑tuning the beta parameter. Great for students and engineers experimenting with attribute control.

blogs.title: Limitations, Open Questions and Research Directions After DPO
blogs.description: A thoughtful essay for researchers and advanced practitioners outlining open problems from the paper: OOD generalization of DPO policies, scaling to 100B+ models, interaction with synthetic preference generation/self‑labeling, theoretical links to other preference/RL formalisms, and ethical considerations of simplifying RLHF. Suggests experiments and possible improvements to explore.
